cim: 3 charged with using AI to commit $129 million in fraud
cim_eredeti: 3 charged with using AI to commit $129 million in fraud
szoveg_eredeti:
Nov. 6 (UPI) -- Three foreign nationals were arrested and charged with using artificial intelligence to steal more than $129 million from businesses, the U.S. Attorney's Office announced.

Three men, Jacob Soall, 41, of Marbella, Spain and Britain; Sharon Hazan, 54, of Israel; and Guy Sheetrit, 42, of Israel and the United Arab Emirates, are each charged with seven offenses, including fraud, identity theft and money laundering, according to a press release from the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Southern District of New York.

The scheme allegedly included using artificial intelligence to call companies and impersonate the voices and images of corporate executives at several companies and attorneys at major law firms in order to trick employees into sending large payments to bank accounts all over the world controlled by members of the group, the indictment said.

The group allegedly stole from companies all over the United States and the world. They include more than $4.8 million from a hospital system in Missouri, more than $2.6 million from a bank headquartered in Rhode Island, more than $2.9 million from a hospital system in California, more than $11.5 million from a financial technology company based in Britain, more than $4.6 million from a mutual fund company based in Massachusetts and $5.2 million from a pet food company based in Florida.

They directed the victims to wire money to bank accounts controlled by conspirators all over the world, including in the United States, Spain, Portugal, Greece, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Austria, Slovakia and China, the press release said.

Once the money had been wired, the men and their co-conspirators allegedly converted it into cryptocurrency and distributed it among themselves and their co-conspirators.

"[AI] technology offers tremendous potential. But the public should recognize that there are some who seek to use this emerging technology to pursue criminal goals," said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald in a statement. "I encourage individuals and the business community to consider how to best protect themselves from the emerging threat of [AI]-enabled crime."

"The alleged scheme orchestrated by Soall, Hazan and Sheetrit demonstrates how the use of advanced technology can be exploited to commit large-scale fraud," said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle Jr. in a statement.
